headline: Broad Rally Closes Friday on a Sour Weekly Note as Iran Risk and Tariff Shock Set the Agenda
body_html:
Equities managed a constructive finish to Friday's session, with roughly 370 names advancing against 175 declining across the 549-stock universe — a healthy two-to-one breadth ratio that nonetheless failed to rescue the broader week. Materials led all sectors, adding 1.48%, driven in part by a sharp 8.09% surge in Alpha Metallurgical Resources and a 6.75% gain in Albemarle, the lithium specialist, signalling renewed appetite for commodity-linked names. Homebuilders followed at 1.14%, while Software and Healthcare posted gains just under 1%.

The session's shadow was cast by Semiconductors, the only sector to finish in the red at -0.23%, where Marvell Technology shed 5.57% and weighed on the group. Infrastructure-adjacent names also retreated — Quanta Services fell 3.49% — suggesting some profit-taking in capital-intensive plays that had run hard earlier in the year. Bond yields and Iran-related geopolitical uncertainty were cited as twin drags keeping the weekly scorecard negative despite Friday's recovery.

Heading into the new week, traders face a crowded docket of geopolitical flashpoints: the collapse of U.S.-Canada trade negotiations has triggered a fresh wave of tariffs, while rising tensions over potential new Iran sanctions are lifting oil and adding a risk premium to global markets. How those cross-currents resolve will likely set the tone through month-end.

briefs.headline: U.S.-Canada Trade Talks Break Down, Tariffs Snap Into Effect
briefs.body: Negotiations between Washington and Ottawa ended without agreement over the weekend, triggering a new round of bilateral tariffs that analysts warn could ripple through North American supply chains. The development adds to an already unsettled trade backdrop and is expected to weigh on cross-border industrial and consumer names when markets reopen Monday.

briefs.headline: Oil Climbs as Fresh Iran Sanctions Threat Stokes Supply Anxiety
briefs.body: Crude prices moved higher Friday after reports that the Trump administration is preparing another round of sanctions targeting Iran's energy partners. The prospect of tighter Persian Gulf supply drove buying in energy-linked assets, though the sector itself posted only a modest 0.22% advance as investors balanced the geopolitical premium against demand uncertainty.

briefs.headline: Iran Permits Iraqi Tankers Through Strait of Hormuz
briefs.body: Tehran signalled a selective easing of Hormuz transit restrictions, granting passage to a number of Iraqi oil vessels. The move was seen as a tactical gesture rather than a broad de-escalation, and came even as Iran publicly condemned U.S. plans to expand sanctions, keeping geopolitical risk elevated heading into the week.

briefs.headline: Israeli Strikes in Southern Syria Rattle Regional Stability
briefs.body: Israeli forces struck targets in southern Syria on Friday, drawing a sharp condemnation from Damascus. Separately, Syria's foreign minister suggested security dialogue with Israel could resume despite what he described as an absence of mutual trust — a nuanced signal that diplomatic back-channels remain open even as military activity intensifies.

briefs.headline: Marvell Leads Semiconductor Sector Lower in Friday Drag
briefs.body: Marvell Technology dropped 5.57% on Friday, pulling the broader semiconductor sector into negative territory for the session at -0.23% — the only sector group to close in the red. Power-module specialist Vicor and semi-materials name Qnity Electronics also retreated, suggesting profit-taking across hardware-adjacent names after recent outperformance.

briefs.headline: Nuclear Buildout Tilts Domestic as Developers Shun Import Delays
briefs.body: A growing number of domestic power developers are opting for locally designed reactor configurations to sidestep the procurement and approval delays that have plagued imported nuclear technology. The shift underscores a broader industrial-policy trend toward supply-chain localisation and could benefit domestic engineering and construction contractors in the quarters ahead.
